frequency_THz.note: hyperfine centre of gravity; derived from the printed FTS transition energy 24360.790(1) cm^-1. The paper also gives nu_MOT = 730.31682(3) THz, which is the F=11 -> F'=12 component including a -22(2) MHz MOT detuning
frequency_THz.source: Hostetter, Pritchard, Lawler, Saffman, Phys. Rev. A 91, 012507 (2015)

wavenumber_cm.source: Hostetter, Pritchard, Lawler, Saffman, Phys. Rev. A 91, 012507 (2015)

loss_rate_upper_limit_s.note: UPPER LIMIT (bound): gamma_ms + gamma_la from MOT decay vs excited-state fraction; branching to metastable states ~1e-6, total leakage out of the cooling transition ~1e-5 (dominated by Raman transitions to other ground hyperfine levels)
loss_rate_upper_limit_s.source: Miao, Hostetter, Stratis, Saffman, Phys. Rev. A 89, 041401(R) (2014)

Gamma1_buffer_gas_MOT_s.note: decay rate to metastable states in a buffer-gas-loaded MOT (higher He background)
Gamma1_buffer_gas_MOT_s.source: Hemmerling, Drayna, Chae, Ravi, Doyle, New J. Phys. 16, 063070 (2014) (arXiv:1310.3239), Table 1

estimated_E1_leak_s.note: rough hydrogenic estimate for the only single-electron-allowed decay, to 4f11 5d6s (1D) J=17/2, 475 cm^-1 below the cooling level
estimated_E1_leak_s.source: Miao, Hostetter, Stratis, Saffman, Phys. Rev. A 89, 041401(R) (2014)

leak_to_metastable.repump: self-repumped: cooling light also repumps F=10 (99.9% of population in F=11); a separate F=10 -> F'=11 repumper mainly traps additional atoms (Miao 2014)

not_found: Isotope shifts: not applicable, 165Ho is the only stable isotope

Lifetime of the drawn level 15136.06 cm^-1 (J=15/2, 660.7 nm) and of the metastable 4f11 6s2 4Io13/2 level at 5419.70 cm^-1: not in Den Hartog et al. 1999 (lowest level 16709.82); Miao 2014 only mentions calculated M1 lifetimes of 0.02-0.24 s for the ground-term levels without assigning them

Linewidths of the narrow cycling lines at 1193 nm (8378.91), 867.3 nm (11530.56), 660.9 nm (15130.31) and 545.3 nm (18337.80 cm^-1): listed as unknown in Miao 2014 Table I; no later measurement located; no narrow-line Ho MOT paper located

Hyperfine constants of excited levels other than the 410.5 nm level (e.g. 16709.82, 24014.22): the hfs literature (Burghardt et al. Z. Phys. A 307, 193 (1982); Newman et al. PRA 83, 012713 (2011); Kroeger/Stefanska/Furmann/Basar series) was not accessible; only the Burghardt abstract was read (4I11/2 measured, Q = 2.716(9) b, no A/B values in the abstract)
Measured Lande g factors of excited levels: none located (NIST lists very few for Ho I)
Den Hartog 1999 Table 1 (39 odd-parity levels, 26143-41256 cm^-1) was read once but not entered: none of those levels is drawn on the site and the read could not be cross-checked
Remaining ~280 lines of Nave 2003 Table 2 (lower levels other than 0 and 5419.70 cm^-1): not transcribed
Absolute frequencies of lines other than 410.5 nm: none located
conflicts: 410.5 nm line A: 2.04(10)e8 s^-1 (Nave 2003, adopted; lifetime 4.9 ns, 32.5 MHz) vs 1.55e8 s^-1 in the NIST lines file; earlier lifetime 6.3(5) ns ("Other" column of Den Hartog 1999)

NIST A values for the other strong blue lines are likewise 10-25% below Nave 2003: 405.4 nm 1.62e8 vs 2.00(10)e8; 416.3 nm 8.97e7 vs 1.06(5)e8; 417.3 nm 2.58e7 vs 3.12(16)e7; 404.1 nm 3.73e7 vs 4.48(22)e7; 425.4 nm 1.15e7 vs 1.00(5)e7 (here NIST is higher); 598.3 nm 9.3e5 vs 9.2(5)e5 (agree)
410.5 nm level energy: 24360.790(1) cm^-1 (Hostetter 2015, FTS centre of gravity) vs 24360.81 NIST
Ionization potential: 48565.910(3) cm^-1 (published abstract, adopted) vs 48565.939(4) / 48565.909(3) in the arXiv v1 text vs 48567(5) NIST
Leak rate of the 410.5 nm line to metastable states: < 300(100) s^-1 (Miao 2014) vs 1510(203) s^-1 (Hemmerling 2014, buffer-gas MOT)

Level energies modified by Den Hartog 1999 relative to NIST: 29642.95 (NIST 29642.6; Nave: 5419.70 + 24222.90 = 29642.60), 32039.69 (NIST 32039.76), 32785.21 (NIST 32784.83), 34366.10 (NIST 34366.07), 23955.68 (NIST 23955.69); Nave prints 24263.88 for the level NIST and Den Hartog give as 24263.96
Ground-state hyperfine constants: uncorrected A'=800.583645(6), B'=-1668.00527(33) MHz (entered) vs second-order-corrected A=800.583173(36), B=-1668.07870(330) MHz (same paper)
notes: 165Ho has I=7/2; hyperfine convention E = A K/2 + B [3K(K+1)/4 - I(I+1)J(J+1)] / [2I(2I-1)J(2J-1)], K = F(F+1)-I(I+1)-J(J+1) (ground state F=4..11, cooling on F=11 -> F'=12). The Den Hartog et al. 1999 lifetime table and the Nave 2003 transition-rate table were read from the publisher abstract pages, whose HTML embeds the tables, through an automated page reader (direct download is captcha-blocked), not from the PDFs; the even-parity lifetime table was read twice with identical results, every row was matched to a NIST level by energy and J, and the Nave A values reproduce 1/tau for the single-branch levels (e.g. 204e6 s^-1 <-> 4.9 ns, 0.92e6 <-> 1090 ns). Lifetime uncertainties are the blanket +-5% (+-10%/+-15% where footnoted). Nave wavelengths quoted in notes are air wavelengths. Extra fields beyond SCHEMA.md: top-level ionization_limit; level fields lifetime_other, level_energy_measured, C_kHz/D_kHz inside the ground-state hyperfine entry; transition fields linewidth_MHz / linewidth_kHz, wavenumber_cm, leak_to_metastable, alternatives. rme_J_ea0 values are derived from the Nave A coefficient of the same entry (schema convention, J' = upper level). g_J without a literature source is copied from the NIST levels file (few exist for Ho I).
